fetch.note: Days with >= 0.10 in. Replaces humidity_monthly: NOAA's normals publish no moisture variable beyond precipitation, so the humidity figures could not have come from the source they cited. This is a rain-frequency measure and the captions describe it as such — it is not a humidity substitute.

captions: {city} sees measurable rain on about {total} days a year, most often in {peak}. Wet spells put the load on a dryer and a dehumidifier at the same time, which is when a worn heating element or a blocked vent finally shows itself.
Rain falls on roughly {total} days a year in {city}, {SS}, peaking in {peak}. Laundry that cannot dry outdoors goes through the machine instead, so the wettest months are when dryers work hardest.
{city} records measurable rain on about {total} days a year. The damp stretches are when moisture problems surface indoors, and when a dryer that vents poorly starts taking two cycles to do one load.
